newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Sihanouk backs international court for Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk backs international court for Pol Pot.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk said Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot should face an international court, but if that could not be arranged, a Cambodian court was likely to sentence him to life in prison.
"Personally, I reckon that Pol Pot should be tried by an international court for crimes against humanity," the king said in an interview released by the palace on Thursday.
"But in the absence of an international court a Cambodian court could try him in Cambodia itself," the king said in the interview with his regular bulletin.
Cambodia's two prime ministers announced on Saturday that Pol Pot had been captured by a breakaway Khmer Rouge faction.

In a rare display of public unity the two premiers sent a letter to the United Nations seeking the world body's help in bringing to justice those responsible for crimes committed during Pol Pot's 1975-79 "killing fields" rule.
The United States later said it would help Cambodia extradite Pol Pot from Cambodia and asked Canada to consider using Canadian law to facilitate the process.
China later hinted that it would not support an international tribunal for Pol Pot.
First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Wednesday the United States and China should not interfere in the Pol Pot affair.
Ranariddh said on Thurday negotiations with the Khmer Rouge breakaway faction holding Pol Pot were continuing.
Sihanouk said Pol Pot could be tried in a Cambodian court if an international tribunal could not be arranged.
"The death penalty being abolished in Cambodia, Pol Pot will certainly be sentenced to a life in prison," he said.
More than one million Cambodians died of starvation or hard labour, or were executed during Pol Pot's rule.
